record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: unbounded extremal solutions in high dimension
record.original_question: Let Omega be a bounded smooth convex set in R^N with N >= 10. For the extremal solution u^* of the nonlinear Dirichlet problem -Delta u = lambda e^u in Omega, u>0 in Omega, u=0 on the boundary, is u^* unbounded? If not for some convex domains, can one choose another smooth increasing convex nonlinearity f with f(0)>0 and f(t)/t -> infinity, possibly depending on Omega, so that the corresponding extremal solution is not in L^infinity(Omega)?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6.1 ([16, 34]). Assume Omega is a bounded smooth convex set in R^N, N >= 10. Let f(u)=e^u. Is u^* unbounded?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded smooth convex domain with $N\geq 10$. For $\lambda>0$ consider the semilinear Dirichlet problem
$$-\Delta u = \lambda e^{u}\ \text{in } \Omega,\qquad u>0\ \text{in } \Omega,\qquad u=0\ \text{on }\partial\Omega.$$
It is classical that there is a critical parameter $\lambda^{*}\in(0,\infty)$ such that for $\lambda\in(0,\lambda^{*})$ the problem has a minimal classical solution $u_{\lambda}$, and for $\lambda>\lambda^{*}$ no solution exists. The extremal solution is defined as $u^{*}(x):=\lim_{\lambda\uparrow\lambda^{*}}u_{\lambda}(x)$; it is the unique weak solution at $\lambda=\lambda^{*}$.

(a) Is $u^{*}\notin L^{\infty}(\Omega)$ for every such $\Omega$?

(b) If (a) fails — i.e., if there exist bounded smooth convex domains $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ with $N\geq 10$ for which the extremal solution of the above problem is bounded — does there exist, possibly depending on $\Omega$, a smooth increasing convex nonlinearity $f:[0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ with $f(0)>0$ and $\lim_{t\to\infty}f(t)/t=\infty$ such that the extremal solution of
$$-\Delta u = \lambda f(u)\ \text{in } \Omega,\quad u>0\ \text{in }\Omega,\quad u=0\ \text{on }\partial\Omega$$
fails to be in $L^{\infty}(\Omega)$?
artifact.category_tag: extremal solutions of semilinear elliptic equations
artifact.status_search_result: For general (not necessarily convex) bounded smooth domains, Cabré–Figalli–Ros-Oton–Serra (2020) proved that stable solutions to semilinear elliptic equations are bounded if and only if $N\leq 9$, settling the regularity threshold in the general setting. On convex domains, however, boundedness of the extremal solution for the exponential nonlinearity in dimensions $N\geq 10$ remains an open question, as does the existence of a convex nonlinearity producing an unbounded extremal solution on every convex domain in high dimension. No published resolution of either part for convex domains was located.

status_evidence.title: Stable solutions to semilinear elliptic equations are smooth up to dimension 9
status_evidence.snippet: Stable solutions are bounded in dimension n ≤ 9; log(1/|x|^2) is a singular stable solution for n ≥ 10.
status_evidence.claim: The threshold $N\leq 9$ is optimal in general, but the convex-domain case in $N\geq 10$ is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Singular extremal solutions to a Liouville-Gelfand type problem with exponential nonlinearity
status_evidence.snippet: There exists a domain and smooth f giving a singular extremal solution when N≥10; sharp since regular for all f,Ω when N≤9.
status_evidence.claim: Singular extremal solutions are known to exist for some (non-convex) domains in N≥10; convex case remains open.

status_evidence.title: The extremal solution for the fractional Laplacian
status_evidence.snippet: Brezis–Vázquez raised the question of when the extremal solution is bounded for general convex f, depending on dimension and domain.
status_evidence.claim: The boundedness question on convex domains has been formulated as an open problem.
